title: Urgent Incident Review - Veridian Health Escalation
header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording: Fireflies AI
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Sofia Alvarez (Veridian CTO), Mark Feldman (Head of ML Ops), Darren Cole (SRE), Ellen Park (Security)
summary: Post-incident follow-up for a production outage on 2025-02-10 affecting Veridian Health inference traffic. Discussed root cause (autoscaling edge case + prefix cache eviction), short-term mitigations, long-term reliability improvements, audit and compliance notes, customer remedies (credits/SLAs), and agreed next steps including a formal postmortem document and prioritized engineering tickets.
topics: Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler + KV cache eviction
action_items: Liam Chen: draft technical postmortem (include timeline, logs, root cause analysis) - due 2025-02-15
Priya Rao: share formal SLA credit proposal and invoice reconciliation - due 2025-02-18
Darren Cole + Liam Chen: run a joint load test against Veridian's representative traffic profile and share results - due 2025-02-20
Ava Martinez: schedule executive follow-up with Sofia and legal to confirm remediation and acceptance criteria - due 2025-02-17
Engineering: add immediate alert for sustained queue growth > 30s and failed fallback handoffs - due 2025-02-14
next_steps: Redwood to send initial postmortem draft (Liam) by 2025-02-15
Agree on SLA credit amount and timing (Priya) by 2025-02-18
Run and share targeted load/chaos tests and confirm mitigations (Liam + Darren) by 2025-02-20
Update runbook and PagerDuty playbook; customer sign-off week of 2025-02-24
Follow-up meeting to review final postmortem and acceptance on 2025-02-25
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. We know this is urgent so we'll go through the timeline, what we saw, and next steps. Sofia, do you want to open with impact?
[00:18] Sofia Alvarez: Yeah thanks Ava. Briefly, our clinical triage inference pipeline saw request failures and high latency from ~02/10 10:12 until 10:45 PST, roughly 33 minutes, with a partial restoration after a rollback. Around 4% of production traffic had errors and several timeouts caused alerts downstream.
[00:38] Mark Feldman: It was mostly the high-priority queues that hit the slow path, and we had to flip to the degraded model bundle which increased costs and slowed throughput.
[00:52] Liam Chen: Quick note, from Redwood logs we saw autoscaler triggered a scale event and some model shards briefly lost prefix cache entries which forced full-token recompute, causing CPU/GPU spike and queueing. Might be a concurrency edge with the continuous-batching logic.
[01:12] Darren Cole: We saw the same in our metrics. There were also a couple of 503s from the inference gateway when fallback attempts exceeded retry limits, so the client saw errors.
[01:30] Ellen Park: From a security/audit perspective, did any data egress or unauthorized access occur? We already scanned and there is no evidence of data leakage, but need the postmortem to include log attestations.
[01:50] Liam Chen: Affirmative, no egress. The traces show internal retries and queue saturation, not data plane failures. But we'll include log slices for the time window.
[02:05] Ava Martinez: Okay, let's walk through the timeline we stitched together. Liam, can you narrate the sequence?
[02:20] Liam Chen: Sure. At 10:09 there was a brief traffic spike — customer-reported sudden batch that was 3x normal for that route. Autoscaler spun up instances, but due to a race the new instances didn't warm the KV cache. Requests that routed to fresh workers missed the prefix cache and fell back to full decode which is ~4-6x heavier. That pushed GPU utilization up and the router started queueing. At 10:28 we hit the retry threshold and some requests were dropped. By 10:35 we triggered a manual rollback to previous model variant which had warmed caches and stabilized.
[02:58] Sofia Alvarez: That race condition — is this on our side of the routing rules or Redwood's autoscale? We need to know ownership.
[03:12] Liam Chen: The initial load pattern came from your side (Veridian batch job), but the cache warm strategy and how new replicas are inserted into the routing ring is a Redwood config/behavior. We should own the service behavior here and propose mitigations.
[03:29] Priya Rao: For transparency, we'll include the config snapshots and the autoscaler logs.
[03:39] Mark Feldman: Also important: our consumers saw a five to ten minute window of degraded latency afterwards even after rollback. Why did it take so long to return to baseline?
[03:54] Liam Chen: A few things — the caches take time to populate; the queue backlog had to drain; and the degraded model variant still had higher per-request time. We didn't have an automatic fast-path to preferentially warm hot prefixes.
[04:18] Darren Cole: Is there a known mitigation to avoid cold-prefix penalties on replica join?
[04:25] Liam Chen: Yes, we have a couple: 1) proactive weave warm-up during scale-up (pre-loading hot prefixes), 2) routing policy to prefer warmed replicas for hot routes, 3) temporary rate-limiter to smooth bursty traffic.
[04:43] Sofia Alvarez: Any chance of automatic fallback to a cheaper but warmed model instead of failing? The degraded model slowed but didn't drop traffic.
[04:53] Liam Chen: We can implement a prioritized fallback that prefers warmed variants; currently fallback is first-available which can pick cold nodes. We'll add that to short-term fixes.
[05:05] Ava Martinez: From the SLA side, Priya, what's our current posture?
[05:12] Priya Rao: Veridian is on Standard+ with a 99.9% uptime SLA for the inference route. This incident is likely a breach window. We'll need to propose credits per the contract and agree on acceptance of our remediation.
[05:28] Sofia Alvarez: We will expect full postmortem with logs and a remediation timeline. Also, our legal/security teams want confirmation there was no data exposure.
[05:40] Ellen Park: yes, please include KMS/HSM access logs and SSO artifacts for the time window.
[05:50] Liam Chen: We'll attach KMS logs and access records. No key usage outside normal patterns.
[06:01] Mark Feldman: Can we get a concrete short-term mitigation plan with owners? We need steps that reduce recurrence risk in the next 30 days.
[06:12] Ava Martinez: Let's enumerate: hot-prefix warm-up for scale-up, routing preference for warmed replicas, alert for queue growth and failed fallbacks, improved retry/backoff tuning, and a post-incident runbook update. Who owns each?
[06:27] Liam Chen: Engineering will take warm-up and routing policy. I'll own the ticket to implement prefetch warmers.
[06:34] Priya Rao: I'll manage SLA credit communications and coordinate legal artifacts.
[06:39] Darren Cole: I'll run a joint load test once the changes are ready.
[06:45] Sofia Alvarez: One ask — include an item to show us the cost impact of the degraded fallback. We need to reconcile the billing spike.
[06:55] Priya Rao: We'll include a cost breakdown for the incident window, and if needed a credit.
[07:03] Liam Chen: Technical notes: the continuous-batching module currently aggregates tokens by prefix fingerprint; if a new replica hasn't seen the prefix, the KV cache miss path does a full decode. That is O(n) more work. We need to change the join protocol to hydrate cache entries for the top-N prefixes.
[07:30] Mark Feldman: Also consider safety limits — if queue depth exceeds threshold, we should degrade gracefully rather than consistently retry and impact downstream.
[07:42] Liam Chen: Agree. Implementing circuit-breakers at the router and per-route QoS is on the roadmap. We can expedite for Veridian's routes.
[07:56] Ava Martinez: Let's talk about monitoring — what failed to alert?
[08:02] Darren Cole: Our alerting was noisy, but didn't capture the warm-cache misses specifically. We saw high GPU % and retries but no single signal flagged the prefix warm miss pattern.
[08:16] Liam Chen: We'll add a metric for prefix-miss rate and a derived alert when miss rate increases together with queue latency.
[08:26] Ellen Park: Regarding compliance notes, add audit log attestations and confirm retention windows—we may need extended retention for this account for a month.
[08:36] Priya Rao: We can increase log retention for the affected window and provide attestations.
[08:42] Sofia Alvarez: What about a customer-facing runbook? We don't want to be surprised again.
[08:50] Ava Martinez: We'll produce a joint runbook with steps for both teams — e.g., throttling strategy, contact points, and rollback triggers.
[09:00] Mark Feldman: One procedural ask: give us a simple decision tree — if prefix miss spike > X and queue depth > Y, then we do Z. Clear thresholds.
[09:12] Liam Chen: We'll propose thresholds and invite Veridian to validate with their traffic profile.
[09:20] Sofia Alvarez: On the legal front, our counsel will review the credit and the postmortem; we'll need that by 2025-02-18.
[09:30] Priya Rao: Noted.
[09:34] Ava Martinez: Any blockers to the proposed action items?
[09:37] Darren Cole: Only time — we'll need a dev window and coordination for load tests.
[09:42] Liam Chen: We'll spin a small-canary patch for the warm-up in the next sprint and run it in staging.
[09:48] Sofia Alvarez: Please mark all changes as urgent and communicate schedule. We prefer timed updates.
[09:55] Ava Martinez: We'll send progress updates every 48 hours until closure.
[10:02] Liam Chen: Quick technical caveat — it's possible the miss rate is exacerbated by an unintended client-side fan-out pattern; we should instrument client routing to validate that your batch job isn't fan-outting requests.
[10:20] Mark Feldman: We'll audit our job; thanks.
[10:25] Priya Rao: Recap of immediate deliverables: postmortem draft, SLA credit proposal, load-test plan, runbook update, and alerting changes.
[10:38] Sofia Alvarez: We appreciate the responsiveness. Final ask: include a slide deck or short one-page summary for our execs.
[10:47] Ava Martinez: We'll include an exec summary with timeline and remediation.
[10:52] Liam Chen: I'll attach log snippets and sample traces to the postmortem draft.
[10:58] Ava Martinez: Ok let's close. We'll reconvene on 2025-02-25 after the postmortem. Thanks everyone.
[11:06] End of recording (approx 54 minutes)
